Here's the full record of what Argus did, in order:

**Investigation (14:15:37–14:15:45 UTC)**
- Picked up the HighErrorRate alert on io-shop and moved the incident to INVESTIGATING, then called in the Investigator Agent.
- Pulled 360 minutes of per-minute metrics for the service and placed the incident start at 14:10.
- Recorded where the three replicas run (io-shop-7d9c4f8b6-x2k9p, -m4q7r and -c8v2n, all on Tesla-V100-SXM2-16GB).
- Queried production change events (deploys/releases) and service logs, and got 0 results back for both.
- Formed one candidate cause and read every channel available. The Mitigation Agent checked the flag provider's history and found 1 recent flag change.

**Mitigation (14:15:46–14:17:06 UTC)**
- Moved the incident to MITIGATING and called in the Mitigation Agent, which reverted the feature flag `monthly-spend-feature`.
- Watched the service for up to 120s; it was not at baseline on the first check, and at 14:17:06 it was confirmed back at baseline since 14:16. The action was judged CONFIRMED and the incident moved to MITIGATED, since the rule that paged had stopped firing.

**Follow-up (14:17:12–14:17:14 UTC)**
- The Code-Fix Agent opened a draft pull request with a proposed fix: https://github.com/ohadraz/Argus-Demo-Target-App/pull/101
- Argus filed what was tried on the incident (putting `monthly-spend-feature` back), and the Postmortem Agent wrote the postmortem, attributing the errors to an unguarded division in `src/io_shop/spend_summary.py:47` raising ZeroDivisionError on the account page path when the flag was rolled out to 100%. Estimated customer loss was put at USD 1,808.92.

One thing to flag: the record contains inconsistent timestamps (the event log runs around 14:10–14:17, while the postmortem narrates the same sequence at 21:35–21:42 on 28 September), and the record does not say why.
